parts.visual:
A 'Pivot' occurs when a company realizes its current business model is failing, and completely changes direction to survive.

The Anatomy of a Pivot:
1. The Sunk Cost Fallacy: The dangerous executive mindset of continuing a bad project just because you already spent millions on it.
2. The Core Asset: Pivoting is not starting from scratch; it is taking your best technology and pointing it at a different customer.
3. The Burn Rate: You must pivot before you run out of cash.
parts.audio: A pivot is a radical shift in business strategy to save a failing company. Executives must overcome the Sunk Cost Fallacy and pivot before the company runs out of cash.

questions.question: Your video game company spent $10 million building a game that nobody is playing. However, the internal chat system you built for the game is incredible. What is the executive move?
options: Spend another $10 million trying to make the game popular.
Pivot. Shut down the game, package the chat system as a standalone B2B product, and sell it to other companies.
questions.correct_answer: Pivot. Shut down the game, package the chat system as a standalone B2B product, and sell it to other companies.
questions.explanation: This is exactly how Slack was created. They pivoted away from a failing game to sell their internal communication tool.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO. What cognitive bias is she fighting?
questions.tts_text: I know we spent two years building this hardware, but the market has shifted to software. We have to kill the hardware division today, no matter how much it hurts.
questions.explanation: Money already spent is 'sunk' (gone forever). You cannot make future decisions based on money you cannot get back.

questions.question: Why is 'Burn Rate' critical when deciding to pivot?
options: Because pivoting requires building a fire.
Because a pivot takes time to execute. If you wait until you only have 2 weeks of cash left, the pivot will fail. You must pivot while you still have runway.
questions.correct_answer: Because a pivot takes time to execute. If you wait until you only have 2 weeks of cash left, the pivot will fail. You must pivot while you still have runway.
questions.explanation: A pivot is a race against the clock. The earlier you recognize failure, the higher your chance of survival.

questions.question: When a company pivots, what usually happens to the existing staff?
options: Massive restructuring. The engineers who built the old product might not have the skills needed for the new product, leading to layoffs.
questions.correct_answer: Massive restructuring. The engineers who built the old product might not have the skills needed for the new product, leading to layoffs.
questions.explanation: A true pivot is a brutal, emotional process. It is the ultimate test of executive resolve.

pairs.match: A fundamental change in a business strategy to prevent failure
Money that has already been spent and cannot be recovered
The speed at which a company spends its cash reserves
The number of months a company can survive before running out of money
